source: When the elevator is unavailable, people who need step-free access should use the east entrance. A ramp leads from that entrance to the meeting room. The west door will stay unlocked, but there are stairs between it and the meeting room. A staff member will be at the east door from 9 a.m.
revision: Use the east entrance for step-free access while the elevator is out. A ramp connects that entrance to the meeting room, and a staff member will be at the door from 9 a.m. You can still enter through the west door, though you'll need to take the stairs to reach the meeting room.

source: The new bus schedule will go into effect on Saturday. Buses will run every 20 minutes on the main road until 7 p.m. After that time they will run every 40 minutes. The last bus will leave the station at 10:30 p.m., which is the same time it leaves under the current schedule.
revision: Starting Saturday, expect a bus on the main road every 20 minutes until 7 p.m. After that, buses will come every 40 minutes. The last departure from the station stays at 10:30 p.m.

source: I had already replaced the batteries when I realized the remote still wasn't working. When I opened the back again, I could see that a small piece of paper was caught between a battery and the metal contact. I pulled out the paper and the remote worked the next time I pressed a button.
revision: New batteries hadn't fixed the remote, so I took the back off again. A scrap of paper was wedged between a battery and its metal contact. I removed it, pressed a button, and this time the remote worked.

source: The price of the small package is lower, but the larger package contains enough material for two full repairs. We only expect to carry out one repair this month. The supplier says the larger package can be stored for later use as long as the container has not been opened.
revision: We expect to do just one repair this month. The smaller package costs less, while the larger one holds enough for two complete repairs. According to the supplier, the larger package can be kept for later if its container stays sealed.

source: The workshop starts with a demonstration that lasts 15 minutes. Attendees then work in pairs using tools provided at each table. The instructor will answer questions as people work. Anyone who does not finish the exercise can take the remaining materials home, but the tools must stay in the room.
revision: After a 15-minute demonstration, attendees pair up and use the tools on their table. The instructor answers questions during the exercise. If you need more time, you can take the leftover materials home and finish there. Leave the tools in the room.

source: Ravi recorded the temperature every hour while Nina inspected the seals at the end of each shift. Nina did not see a leak during those inspections. Ravi reported that the temperature went above the target twice. The next test will check whether those changes occur after the door is left open.
revision: During the test, Ravi took an hourly temperature reading and Nina checked the seals at shift end. Ravi noted two readings above the target. Nina found no leaks in her inspections. In the next test, the team will look for a link between a door left open and those temperature changes.

source: The parking lot has fewer spaces during construction, so visitors may need to park on nearby streets. There is still room to drop off passengers by the entrance. The accessible parking spaces beside the entrance will stay open. Construction is scheduled to finish in June, although rain could delay the work.
revision: Construction has reduced the number of parking spaces. You may need to park on the street, but you can still drop off passengers at the entrance. The accessible spaces next to the entrance remain open. The work is due to finish in June, weather permitting.

source: The garden group plans to grow herbs next to the path because people will be able to pick them without walking into the planted area. Tomatoes will go against the wall, where they receive more afternoon sun. Before planting the tomatoes, the group needs to replace a damaged section of the fence.
revision: The group wants people to be able to pick herbs from the path, so the herbs will grow along its edge. The wall gets more sun in the afternoon, which makes it the spot for the tomatoes. The group needs to repair part of the fence before putting the tomatoes in.

source: The report gives two reasons for the delay. Early versions of the form asked people to enter the same information twice, and some applications arrived without the required signature. The new form removes the duplicate questions. Applicants are still responsible for signing the form before they send it.
revision: According to the report, two issues slowed things down: the old form repeated questions, and some people sent it in unsigned. The replacement form asks for the information once. Applicants still need to sign before submitting it.

source: We knocked on the door three times before anyone answered. A woman opened the door and asked whether we were there to collect the table. We told her we were looking for a different address. She pointed to a house across the street and said its number was hard to see from the pavement.
revision: On our third knock, a woman came to the door and asked if we'd come for the table. We said we were looking for another address. She pointed across the street to a house whose number, she said, was difficult to see from the pavement.

source: There are two ways to pay for a replacement card. You can pay in person at the front desk, or you can ask for a link by email. The office does not accept cash by post. After payment, staff will hold the card for collection for up to 14 days.
revision: Pay at the front desk or request an emailed payment link for your replacement card. Don't send cash through the post. Once you've paid, the office will keep the card for you to collect for up to 14 days.

source: The students remembered more words after practicing in small groups, but the groups also had more time to practice. We cannot tell whether the group format accounted for the improvement. A second study will give each group the same amount of time and use the same word list for everyone.
revision: Small-group practice was followed by better recall, though those students got more practice time as well. The results cannot isolate the effect of the group format. In the second study, every group will get the same practice time and work from one word list.

source: The printer for the second floor is out of service until a replacement part arrives. Staff can use the printer in the ground-floor copy room. It is important to collect documents with personal information as soon as they print. Ordinary print jobs can be picked up later in the day.
revision: Until the part arrives, send your jobs to the ground-floor copy room. The second-floor printer is down. Pick up anything with personal information as soon as it comes out of the printer. You can leave routine jobs there until later in the day.

source: The kitchen starts preparing breakfast at 6 a.m., but staff do not open the dining room until 7 a.m. Anyone leaving earlier can order a packed breakfast the previous evening. The order must include the time of departure and any food allergies. Packed breakfasts are collected at reception.
revision: The kitchen starts work at 6 a.m. The dining room opens an hour later, at 7 a.m. If you're leaving before then, order a packed breakfast the night before and tell staff when you leave and whether you have any food allergies. Pick it up at reception.

source: The footbridge is narrow, and riders sometimes meet people coming the other way near the middle. The council recommends walking bikes across the bridge during busy periods. It has not decided whether to build a wider crossing. Staff will count pedestrians and cyclists on weekends before putting forward a proposal.
revision: People approaching from opposite sides sometimes meet halfway across the narrow footbridge. When it's busy, the council advises cyclists to get off and walk their bikes across. A wider crossing is still undecided. Staff will count weekend pedestrian and bicycle traffic before proposing a change.

source: I meant to drop off the keys before the office closed, but the bus was late and I got there a few minutes after closing. The notice on the door gave a number to call after hours. I called, and the caretaker told me to leave the keys in an envelope beside the side entrance.
revision: The late bus got me to the office a few minutes after closing, so I couldn't hand in the keys as planned. I rang the after-hours number on the door. The caretaker asked me to put the keys in an envelope and leave it by the side entrance.

source: The contract allows the tenant to paint one room if the landlord first approves the color in writing. The tenant cannot remove built-in shelving. At the end of the lease, the landlord will inspect the room before deciding whether the walls need to be painted again. The contract does not say who would carry out that work.
revision: To paint one room, the tenant needs written approval of the color from the landlord. Built-in shelves have to stay. The landlord will inspect the room when the lease ends and then decide whether the walls need repainting. The contract leaves open who would do the painting.

source: The first batch hardened before the pieces could be removed from the molds. The technician used the same mixture in the second batch but took the pieces out earlier, while they were still soft. Those pieces kept their shape as they cooled. The team will repeat the test before changing the written instructions.
revision: In the first batch, the mix set before anyone could take the pieces out of the molds. The technician left the recipe unchanged for the second batch and removed the pieces sooner, while they were soft. They held their shape while cooling. The team wants to repeat the test before revising the instructions.

source: The gallery has enough space for the larger display, but its lighting would need to be adjusted to protect the prints. The smaller display could use the existing lighting. Neither display requires alterations to the walls. The curator will decide after comparing what each display can show and how much staff time it takes to install.
revision: Both displays fit without changes to the walls. The larger one fits in the gallery but would need different lighting to protect the prints, whereas the smaller one could use the lights already in place. The curator will weigh what each option can show against the staff time needed for installation.

source: People attending the lecture do not need to book a seat. A separate registration form is required for the discussion afterward because that room has limited space. Registration for the discussion closes on Wednesday. Anyone who only wants to hear the lecture can arrive on the day and go straight to the auditorium.
revision: You can go straight to the auditorium on the day of the lecture without booking. To join the discussion afterward, register separately by Wednesday. There are only so many places in the discussion room.

source: The theater will keep the earlier performance if enough people book by Friday. If the earlier performance is canceled, anyone with a ticket can move to the later show or ask for a refund. Tickets for the later show will remain valid. The box office will email everyone who booked the earlier performance.
revision: Friday's booking numbers will determine whether the early performance goes ahead. The box office will email everyone booked for that show. If it is canceled, those ticket holders can switch to the later performance or request a refund. Tickets already booked for the later show stay valid.

source: The guide recommends starting at the south gate because the path rises gently from that side. The route is shorter from the north gate, but it includes a steep section by the stream. Both routes lead to the same viewpoint. The guide says walkers should turn back if the stepping stones are underwater.
revision: Both gates lead to the same viewpoint. The guide suggests the south gate for its gentle climb. Starting in the north is quicker by distance, but that route has a steep stretch beside the stream. If water covers the stepping stones, the guide advises turning around.

source: The room contains desks on wheels, which makes it possible to clear the floor for group activities. Staff should bring the desks back into rows after each session. Visitors can sit at any available desk, but bags must stay out of the aisle. There is a shelf by the door for bags.
revision: The desks roll out of the way when a group needs open floor space. After each session, staff should put them back in rows. Visitors can choose any free desk, and the shelf by the door keeps bags out of the aisle.

source: Jordan wrote “West gate” on the delivery note and gave it to the courier. The courier did not use the entrance beside the cafe because its ramp was closed. The shipment reached the west gate at 3 p.m. The receiving team recorded the time and placed the boxes in the storage room.
revision: The courier had a delivery note from Jordan marked “West gate.” With the cafe entrance ramp closed, the courier skipped that entrance. The shipment arrived at the west gate at 3 p.m. The receiving team logged the arrival and moved the boxes into storage.

source: The teacher will hand out the instructions before the pupils open their materials. Each group must count the pieces before it starts. If any pieces are missing, pupils should ask the teacher for replacements. At the end of the lesson the groups will put unused pieces into envelopes and return them to the teacher.
revision: Leave the materials closed until the teacher gives out the instructions. Before starting, each group must count its pieces and ask the teacher for replacements if any are missing. When the lesson ends, put any unused pieces in envelopes and hand them back to the teacher.

source: The walkway becomes slippery after heavy rain, especially near the bottom of the steps. Volunteers can spread gravel on the path, but they may not work on the steps without supervision. The site manager will inspect the area on Monday and decide whether the path needs to close for repairs.
revision: Heavy rain can leave the walkway slick, particularly at the foot of the steps. Volunteers can put gravel on the path. Work on the steps requires supervision. On Monday, the site manager will look over the area and decide whether to close the path for repairs.
